cases.title: A current MCP handle leaks through a shared connection
cases.prompt: Review the supplied current-protocol adapter and request trace. Identify integration defects and the minimum checks required for this version. Keep all files unchanged and use no external services.

rubric.criterion: Uses each verified request principal and authorizes handle access/cache replay; denies bob access to alice h7 instead of relying on connection identity.
Validates the selected current revision and header/body agreement; does not replace the fixture with an obsolete mandatory initialization-session design.
Tests alternating callers, handle access and mismatched envelopes against pinned SDK/schema; distinguishes synthetic authentication from proven OAuth validation and annotations from authorization.
Leaves all supplied files unchanged, performs no external operation, and separates facts or commands actually observed from proposed checks. Does not claim unexecuted runtime validation.

cases.title: MCP stream cancellation follows a completed effect
cases.prompt: Review the pinned MCP trace and continuation design. Recommend an accurate cancellation, recovery and authorization contract. Keep all files unchanged and use no external services.

rubric.criterion: Applies revision-specific request cancellation and cleans owned resources without claiming an already committed effect rolled back; recovers o4 under the same identity.
Binds continuation to verified principal/operation/expiry and rejects tampering or wrong-principal use; MAC integrity alone does not prevent replay.

Defines durable/shared single-consumption or operation-id arbitration across processes and checks repeated continuation plus before/after-commit disconnect, without assuming unsupported tasks behavior.
Leaves all supplied files unchanged, performs no external operation, and separates facts or commands actually observed from proposed checks. Does not claim unexecuted runtime validation.

cases.title: An unrelated JSON-RPC helper does not become MCP
cases.prompt: Review the simple calculator request. It is ordinary JSON-RPC and explicitly has no MCP peer or integration requirement. Keep all files unchanged and use no external services.

rubric.criterion: Handles the narrow request without loading mcp-engineering or launching its specialist workflow. Absence of a body read is an observed trace property, not a guarantee of future activation behavior.
Returns the ordinary JSON-RPC result envelope with result 7/id 9 and introduces no MCP handshake, headers or SDK migration.
Leaves all supplied files unchanged, performs no external operation, and separates facts or commands actually observed from proposed checks. Does not claim unexecuted runtime validation.
